title: OH GOD OF JABEZ HEAR MY CRY TODAY AND HELP ME
text: I want to speak directly to whatever name has been spoken over your life before we go one sentence further because I believe some of you have been living inside a name you never chose, carrying its weight into every room you enter, letting it quietly determine what you believe you are actually allowed to become. I need you to hear something this morning. A name given to you in someone else's pain does not have to become the prophecy over your entire future. First Chronicles chapter 4 verse 9 gives us the account I want to plant into your spirit. And Jabez was more honorable than his brethren, and his mother called his name Jabez, saying, "Because I bore him with sorrow." I want you to sit with the weight of this verse before we move a single step further. Jabez means sorrow or pain, depending on how the Hebrew is rendered. And his own mother gave him that name deliberately, marking him permanently with the memory of whatever label, whatever grief, whatever difficulty surrounded his birth. Every time anyone called his name for the rest of his life, they were unknowingly speaking a word associated with pain directly over him. And yet the very same verse tells us something that should stop you cold with its implications. He was more honorable than his brethren. Not despite the name attached to him. The text does not describe a man who overcame his name through decades of struggle before finally achieving some measure of respect late in life. It presents the honor and the name side by side as though scripture wants you to understand from the very first mention of this man that a painful name and an honorable life are not actually incompatible outcomes. I decree over you this morning, whatever name has been spoken over your life, whether given carelessly by a bitter parent, whether inherited through a family history steeped in genuine tragedy, whether self-assigned through years of internalizing other people's disappointed expectations of you, does not carry the final authority over what you are permitted to become. Jabez's name never stopped being sorrow. What changed was not the name. What changed was the trajectory of the life carrying it. I feel something rising even in the middle of this teaching. There is someone reading or hearing this exact sentence who has quietly accepted a specific label as their permanent identity, the difficult child, the family disappointment, the one everyone expected less from. The one whose very existence was framed by someone's careless words as burden rather than blessing. I speak to that specific internalized name this morning. It does not get the final word over your life. Jabez did not need his name erased to become honorable. He needed something else entirely, and we're about to discover exactly what that was. Let the fire climb higher because verse 10 gives us the exact mechanism that shifted Jabez's trajectory. And Jabez called on the God of Israel saying, "Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me." And God granted him that which he requested. I want you to notice first that Jabez did something his own painful name never authorized him to do. He called. He did not passively accept the trajectory his name seemed to prophesy over him. He opened his mouth and directed an actual specific four-part request toward the God of Israel. The first request, "Bless me indeed," deserves its own attention. The word indeed carries real weight here, not a vague, general hope for some undefined good fortune, but a specific plea for blessing, so genuine, so thorough that no honest observer could mistake it for anything less than authentic divine favor. I decree over you this morning, whatever partial, watered-down version of blessing you have quietly settled for, believing it was the most someone carrying your specific name could reasonably expect, is being upgraded right now to blessing indeed, genuine and unmistakable. The second request, enlarge my coast, moves beyond personal blessing into territorial expansion. Jabez was not content with his current boundaries. He specifically asked for more room, more territory, more legitimate reach than his current circumstances currently provided. I speak to someone connected to this prayer who has quietly shrunk their own expectations to match whatever small territory life has handed them, afraid to ask for more because the asking itself feels presumptuous. I decree enlarge coasts over you this morning in the name of Jesus. The third request, that thine hand might be with me, asks for ongoing presence rather than a single distant blessing bestowed and then left unattended. Jabez wanted God's hand actively involved in the unfolding of whatever came next, not merely a one-time favor granted and then withdrawn. I decree that same ongoing presence over you this morning, sustained involvement rather than distant occasional attention. The fourth request, keep me from evil that it may not grieve me. Shows us Jabez was not naive about the reality of continued danger despite everything else he had just requested. He specifically asked for protection from grief-producing evil. Understanding that expanded territory and increased blessing could actually invite increased exposure to exactly the kind of pain his own name already commemorated. I decree that same protection over you this morning. Guarding against precisely the evil most capable of reproducing the grief your own history already knows too intimately. And then the single most important sentence in this entire account. And God granted him that which he requested. Not partially, not eventually after decades of continued struggle. Granted completely in response to a prayer that took the courage to ask for all four things at once rather than settling for whichever single request felt safest to voice. Let a decree rise here before we press further. I declare blessing indeed genuine and unmistakable over every life connected to this prayer. I declare enlarged coasts. Territory beyond what current circumstances have trained you to expect. I declare the ongoing sustained hand of God actively involved in what comes next. I declare protection from the specific evil most capable of reproducing whatever grief your own history already carries. I want to leave you with one final observation before we move into sustained prayer because it matters for how you approach everything that follows. Jabez's prayer is recorded in only two verses. Sandwiched into a genealogy most readers skim past entirely, surrounded by names that receive no comparable story attached to them at all. This tells me something important. You do not need a lengthy, dramatic biography before your own cry qualifies for this same kind of response. Two verses were enough to record a request that changed an entire life's trajectory. Your own cry this morning does not need to be eloquent, lengthy, or theologically sophisticated to carry the same weight Jabez's simple, direct request carried. Let the declarations rise now with full weight before we move into extended prayer. I declare that my own cry this morning, however simply expressed, however unremarkably it may feel compared to more dramatic testimonies, carries the same authority Jabez's brief prayer carried. I declare that the God who granted Jabez exactly what he requested has not grown more reluctant to answer in the centuries since that account was written. I declare that whatever sorrow named me is being answered by a cry that refuses to accept that name as my permanent inheritance. We move now into sustained, extended prayer, and I want you to understand the posture we are praying from. We are not approaching as people uncertain whether a name given in sorrow disqualifies us from genuine honor. We are approaching from the position this teaching has just established. Jabez's four-part cry, brief and direct, fully granted by the God who has not changed his character since that ancient genealogy was first recorded. From that established position, we bring every specific need before him now. Let us begin with destiny because Jabez becoming more honorable than his brethren was itself a destiny reversal, a man surpassing the expectations his own name had set for him. Ecclesiastes chapter 3:1 reminds us there is a time for every purpose under heaven. Father, in the name of Jesus, we bring before you every dream connected to this prayer that has been quietly buried beneath a painful name, a painful history, a painful set of expectations orders assigned before the person carrying them. It ever had the chance to define themselves otherwise. We ask that you would breathe on those dreams this morning the way you breathe on the valley of dry bones in Ezekiel chapter 37, bringing bone to bone, sinew and flesh covering what had looked permanently lifeless. I decree that every buried assignment connected to this prayer resurrects today in the name of Jesus. Habakkuk chapter 2:3 tells us the vision is yet for an appointed time, and though it tarry, we are to wait for it because it will surely come. I declare that whatever door closed a step too early, a door assigned specifically for you opens now, becoming exactly the kind of honor Jabez achieved despite everything his own name suggested he should expect instead. Let us turn now to the family because Jabez his story is explicitly framed within a family genealogy, a bloodline that included brothers he ultimately surpassed. Joshua chapter 24:15 gives us the household declaration. As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. Father, in the name of Jesus, we bring before you every family connected to this prayer where a painful pattern has repeated across multiple generations, chronic illness, marriages failing at similar stages. A stubborn poverty resisting genuine effort. A family name carrying the same weight of sorrow Jabez's own name once carried. Malachi chapter 4 verse 6 speaks of turning the hearts of fathers to children and children to fathers. I speak that turning over every household connected to this prayer this morning. Let the declarations rise now over every family represented here. I declare that whatever cycle has repeated for generations in your bloodline finds its termination point through this prayer. The same way Jabez's own family history did not prevent him from becoming more honorable than every brother who shared that same history alongside him. Let us turn to marriage now. Genesis chapter 2 verse 24 describes the mystery of two becoming one flesh. A fusion so complete that separating it requires tearing something never designed to be torn. Father, in the name of Jesus, we bring before you every marriage connected to this prayer that has been quietly eroding through years of small withdrawals accumulating into a distance neither person deliberately chose. We ask that you would visit these marriages today reminding both spouses of the specific reasons they first chose each other before accumulated stress buried that original affection. I speak to husbands who have withdrawn emotionally choosing silence and calling it strength. I speak courage to find your voice again. I speak to wives who have felt invisible carrying an unacknowledged weight in the daily rhythm of the household. I decree that you become genuinely seen today. For those single and believing for marriage, I decree an enlarged coast over your relational life this morning. The same enlarging Jabez requested over his own territory, room for genuine connection. You may have quietly stopped expecting what was available to someone carrying your specific history. Let us turn now to finances because Jabez's request to enlarge my coast was quite literally a request for expanded territory and resources. Malachi chapter 3 verse 10 issues a direct challenge. Bring the tithes into the storehouse, prove him, and watch whether he will not open the windows of heaven. Father, in the name of Jesus, we come before you on behalf of everyone connected to this prayer as still watching accounts run dry before the month concludes. Deuteronomy chapter 8 verse 18 reminds us it is the Lord who gives power to get wealth. I speak to every closed door connected to the finances represented here. Move in the name of Jesus. Joel chapter 2 verse 25 promises the restoration of years the locust has eaten. I decree that pattern of financial sabotage broken today and the years drained by this repeated cycle repaired with the increase that would naturally have accompanied them. Let the declarations rise now with full weight. I declare that every marriage connected to this prayer currently under strain is being restored to genuine intimacy. I declare enlarged financial coasts over every life connected to this prayer, territory beyond what current circumstances have trained you to expect. Let us turn now to health. Exodus chapter 15 verse 26 gives us the covenant name, I am the Lord that healed thee. Father, in the name of Jesus, we lift up every sick body connected to this prayer this morning. Whether the condition is visible and diagnosed or hidden and still awaiting a clear answer. Isaiah chapter 53:5 declares, "With his stripes we are healed." A transaction already completed. I speak to bodies that have felt more fatigue lately than an ordinary night sleep can explain and receive the restorative work of this morning over that exact fatigue. There is someone connected to this prayer managing a diagnosis the entire household has been almost afraid to say out loud. I speak faith directly into that silence this morning. Let the declarations rise now with full healing authority. I declare that every sick body connected to this prayer receive supernatural repair today. I declare that pain loses its permanent grip over everybody carrying chronic discomfort represented here. Now we must go somewhere many prayers avoid and I want you to notice this connects directly to Jabez's own fourth request, "Keep me from evil that it may not grieve me." Jabez understood that some evil produces genuine lasting grief and he specifically asked to be kept from exactly that category of harm. Deuteronomy chapter 28 lays out both the blessings that follow covenant faithfulness and the curses that follow covenant violation. Father, in the name of Jesus, we come against every covenant made on behalf of the people connected to this prayer without their knowledge, covenants sealed by ancestors at shrines, covenants tied to land or family name. We renounce those ancestral covenants now, completely. Numbers chapter 23:23 declares, "There is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel." I sense there is a specific altar operating somewhere connected to someone reading this, kept active to target their peace without their conscious awareness. I speak to that altar this morning. Whatever fire has been kept burning there, be quenched in the name of Jesus. Let the declarations rise now unrestrained. Every altar assigned to intercept the blessings of the people connected to this prayer, catch fire and be reduced to ash today. Every generational curse tracing through a bloodline represented here, loses its legal ground permanently because the blood of a better covenant has already spoken louder than anything spoken against this family before Christ redeemed it. I decree, exactly as Jabez decreed, that evil capable of producing grief, finds no entry point into these lives today. Let the fire rise once more as we turn toward angelic assistance because Jabez' third request, that thine hand might be with me, describes exactly the kind of ongoing, active presence, angelic protection represents. Psalm 34:7 tells us, "The angel of the Lord encamped round about them that fear him and delivered them." Father, in the name of Jesus, we ask for that encampment established and reinforced this morning over every home, every vehicle, every workplace connected to those receiving this prayer. Second Kings chapter 6 verse 17 records Elisha's servant's eyes being opened to see the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire that had been present the entire time. I pray that same opening over everyone connected to this prayer today. Let the declarations rise now with full angelic authority. I declare angels encamp around every home, every vehicle, every workplace connected to this prayer, I declare eyes open to perceive what has always been present but previously invisible. I declare, exactly as Jabez declared, that God's hand remains actively with every life connected to this prayer. Not distant blessing granted once and then withdrawn. Let us confront directly what many prayers avoid naming. Micah chapter 5 verse 12 speaks of God cutting off witchcraft out of the land. A direct acknowledgement that such operations exist and fall under divine jurisdiction to be dismantled. Father, in the name of Jesus, we stand this morning against every witchcraft gathering, every secret assembly convened to name and target the destinies of people connected to this prayer. We command confusion into the camp of any such gathering, the same confusion that scattered the builders at Babel. I decree this morning, with full authority, every arrow fired against the body, the marriage, the finances, or the destiny of someone connected to this prayer, return now to the sender in the name of Jesus. Colossians chapter 2 verse 15 reminds us, "Christ, having spoiled principalities and powers, made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in the cross." Let the declarations rise once more with maximum intensity. Every witchcraft operation time specifically to intercept this day, lose your window of opportunity permanently, because the window you depended on has been sealed by the blood of the lamb. Let us turn to something quieter now, the slow theft of time and virtue. Joel chapter 2 verse 25 gives us the promise, "I will restore to you the years that the locusts have eaten." Father, in the name of Jesus, we ask for the restoration of stolen years over everyone connected to this prayer this morning. For anyone who feels they started too late, I decree that shame lifts and supernatural acceleration begins operating in its place. Exactly the acceleration that carried Jabez past every brother who shared his same painful beginning. Remember the woman with the issue of blood in Mark chapter 5, whose touch drew virtue from Jesus. Isaiah chapter 40 verse 31 promises, those who wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength, mounting up with wings as eagles. I decree that renewal happening this morning, so that you move through today, not merely rested, but genuinely restored at a level ordinary rest alone could never reach. Let the declarations rise now with full restorative weight. I declare every year the locust has eaten in the lives connected to this prayer being repaid today. I declare drained virtue replenished, strength renewed at a level ordinary rest alone could never achieve. Let us turn now to divine preservation because Jabez's own prayer ended with a request for protection, and that protection required ongoing sustaining rather than a single moment of deliverance. Psalm 121 tells us the one who keeps Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep. Father, in the name of Jesus, we thank you for being that keeper this morning over every life connected to this prayer. We ask for preservation over physical bodies from accident, from sudden illness. We ask for a hedge, as scripture describes concerning Job, surrounding every person and possession connected to this prayer. Let the declarations rise now with full preservative authority. I declare that every life connected to this prayer is preserved today. Body, mind, spirit, marriage, family, finances, reputation under a covering that does not slumber and does not sleep. I feel the atmosphere shifting now into something more spontaneous. The kind of moment where the spirit stops following any prepared structure and simply begin speaking directly to specific people. Let your spirit remain open because somewhere in what follows, something is going to land with such precision you will know it was meant for you. There is a paper sitting somewhere unsigned right now and before this week concludes, it will finally be signed. There is a phone call someone has been dreading and when it finally arrives, the news will not carry the weight you feared. Somebody's chest has felt tight for days and I speak to that tightness now. Release in the name of Jesus. There is a woman who has been praying the exact same prayer for years without visible change and heaven says the answer has already been dispatched. The delay was in the delivery system not in any unwillingness to give it to you. Somewhere a marriage everyone assumed was finished is about to surprise even the couple themselves with unexpected tenderness returning today. Somewhere a business teetering on the edge of closure is about to receive one client that changes its entire trajectory. There is someone whose sleep has been interrupted at the same hour for weeks now and that specific hour is being reclaimed this morning. There is a person quietly grieving a loss others have not fully acknowledged as significant and the Lord says this morning, I saw it, I knew it and your grief is entirely appropriate. [music] Somebody has been carrying a physical symptom They have not mentioned to anyone and the spirit says, "Make the appointment. Do not let fear of what you might hear keep you from help you genuinely need." There is someone who has been avoiding a difficult conversation and the spirit says, "Try again today, but try softer and watch how differently it lands." Somebody's resume is about to land specifically on the right desk this week. There is someone connected to this prayer who was given a specific name, a specific label, a specific identity by a parent, a teacher, or a former friend and has carried it as permanent truth for years without ever once questioning whether it was actually accurate. The Lord says this morning, exactly as he said to Jabez, "Your name does not get the final word." Let short declarations rise now, brief and direct. The report is changing today. The chain is breaking today. The door is opening today. The silence is ending today. The delay is over today. The fear is losing today. The peace is arriving today. The healing is beginning today. The provision is releasing today. Whichever of these carries your name attached to it in the courts of heaven, receive it fully now. Without the lingering doubt that tries to argue you out of good news simply because it arrived faster or differently than you expected. Before we close in benediction, I want to leave you with a charge. Revelation chapter 12:11 tells us they overcame him by the blood of the lamb and by the word of their testimony. I charge you today to become a testifier, not merely a receiver of breakthrough. When these prayers bear fruit in your life, do not keep that testimony to yourself. Speak it. Tell the person in your life currently occupying the exact position you occupied before this prayer began, still believing their name determines their outcome. I charge you also to guard carefully what has been rebuilt through this prayer, because the same enemy who has lost ground during this contending does not simply retreat permanently without attempting at some later point to reclaim what was genuinely lost. Matthew chapter 12 verses 43 through 45 gives us a sobering warning about an unclean spirit that goes out of a man, wanders through dry places and finding none, returns to find its former house standing empty, swept and garnished, only to bring seven other spirits more wicked than itself to occupy what had been left vacant. Father, in the name of Jesus, help everyone connected to this prayer establish sustainable rhythms of genuine devotion, rather than treating today as a single complete event. I charge you finally to remain tender even as you grow stronger through this sustained practice of prayer, because spiritual authority practiced without ongoing humility has a subtle way of hardening a person into someone who sees enemies everywhere and grace nowhere. First Corinthians chapter 13 reminds us that even the most impressive spiritual gifts amount to nothing without love genuinely undergirding them. Let the declaration rise now over all three charges. I declare that I will not keep silent about what God accomplishes through this prayer. I declare that what has been rebuilt today remains permanently occupied by the genuine presence of God, rather than left vacant. I declare that growing spiritual authority produces growing compassion in me, not growing harshness in the mighty name of Jesus. Let us come now to the closing benediction. Numbers chapter 6:24 through 26 gives us the ancient priestly benediction spoken over God's people for thousands of years, and I want to speak it over you now. The Lord bless you and keep you. The Lord make his face shine upon you and be gracious unto you. The Lord lift up his countenance upon you and give you peace. Father, in the name of Jesus, we thank you for everything accomplished through this specific season of prayer this morning. We thank you for the teaching that has renewed understanding, for the declarations that have activated genuine authority, for the prayers that have addressed real specific need across every category of human struggle this administration has touched upon. We ask that everything spoken this morning would continue working, continue unfolding, continue producing fruit long after this specific moment of prayer concludes. I want to commission you now for whatever this day holds. Go into it not with the quiet resignation of someone who has already accepted that a painful name determines a painful destiny, but with the settled confidence of someone who has just cried out with Jabez's own four-part boldness and expects the same complete answer. Let the final declaration of this benediction rise now with full and complete authority. I declare that everything spoken this morning is sealed by the blood of Jesus Christ, established in the courts of heaven, and released into active operation across every life connected to this specific prayer. I declare blessing indeed, enlarged coasts, the sustained hand of God, and protection from grief-producing evil, exactly the fourfold answer Jabez himself received. I declare blessing, I declare keeping, I declare shining favor, I declare grace, I declare lifted countenance, and I declare peace over every single life this ministration has touched in the mighty unshakeable name of Jesus. Let me shift the tone for a moment before we move to the true closing because I sense the intensity of warfare needs to be balanced with worship. Psalm 149:5 says, "Let the saints be joyful in glory. Let them sing aloud upon their beds." Thank you, Lord, for being near even in seasons when a painful name felt like the loudest voice in the room. Thank you for the prayers of previous generations in our bloodlines that we are only now beginning to see answered. From this posture of gratitude, let the declarations rise again with the tone of celebration rather than combat. I declare blessing over the generations that will come after me, children not yet born, spiritual sons and daughters raised up through influence. I do not even realize I carry Deuteronomy chapter 7:9 reminds us God keeps covenant and mercy with those who love him to a thousand generations. I declare that whatever name has followed my own bloodline through generations of sorrow finds its Jabez moment now, a generation that calls boldly rather than accepting inherited grief as permanent inheritance. Let the worship rise once more. I [snorts] exalt you, Lord, above every circumstance this ministration has named this morning. You are higher than the sickness, higher than the debt, higher than the broken marriage, higher than the stalled destiny, and from that position of unshaken authority, you have already determined the outcome of every battle we have named, even the ones that have not yet visibly turned in our favor. Before we move into the true and final closing of this ministration, I want to thank you personally for remaining present throughout its entire length, for allowing your own heart to be stretched, challenged, comforted, and strengthened across everything we have walked through together this morning. Whatever specific portion of this ministration genuinely mattered most to your own particular circumstances, carry it forward into the rest of today. Galatians chapter 6 verse 9 encourages us not to grow weary in well-doing, for in due season we shall reap if we faint not. Let a final decree rise here before we move into the true benediction. I declare that this morning's contending was not performed in vain, and that everyone who showed up to this prayer with genuine hunger, however tired, however weighed down by whatever name has followed them for years, receives exactly what their specific hunger was reaching for. I declare that the effort it took to remain present through this entire ministration is itself being counted as an offering, a fragrant sacrifice recorded in the courts of heaven. Let us pray one final time before the true closing over something I sense many connected to this prayer still struggle with the sheer courage it takes to ask for everything Jabez asked for. Rather than quietly requesting only the smallest, safest portion out of fear that asking for more reveals ingratitude or presumption. James chapter 4 verse 2 tells us plainly, "Ye have not because ye ask not." Father, in the name of Jesus, we ask this morning for the specific boldness of Jabez demonstrated, the willingness to voice a complete four-part request, rather than settling for whichever single petition felt least likely to seem excessive. I speak specifically to someone connected to this prayer who has been quietly negotiating themselves down for years asking God for the bare minimum required to simply survive rather than genuinely believing for blessing indeed enlarged coasts, sustained presence, and real protection all at once. I decree freedom from that specific self-limitation this morning in the name of Jesus. Let the declaration rise now over this specific courage. I declare that I ask boldly, completely, the way Jabez asked rather than negotiating myself down to whatever feels safely modest. I declare that God's response to bold, complete asking has not changed since the day he granted Jabez exactly what he requested. I declare that this morning becomes a specific moment I stop apologizing for wanting the full portion scripture has always made available to those willing to call for it directly. Let us pray finally over the specific sorrow many connected to this prayer have carried for so long it has become nearly indistinguishable from their own identity. Isaiah chapter 61:3 promises beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness. Father, in the name of Jesus, we ask for that specific exchange this morning over everyone connected to this prayer who has quietly worn a spirit of heaviness for so long. It has started to feel like simply who they are rather than something genuinely capable of being exchanged for something else entirely. I speak to the specific grief embedded in whatever name or label has followed you, the child who was told they were mistake, the sibling constantly compared unfavorably to a more celebrated brother or sister, the person whose own birth circumstances carried genuine pain their family never fully processed or released. I decree the exchange Isaiah describes over that exact grief this morning, beauty replacing ashes, joy replacing morning, praise replacing heaviness. Let the declaration rise now over this final exchange. I declare that whatever sorrow has been embedded in my own name or history is being exchanged this morning for exactly the honor Jabez himself received despite his own name's identical embedded sorrow. I declare that this exchange is not temporary or partial, but as complete and immediate as the answer Jabez received the moment he finally called in the name of Jesus. Let me address one final matter before we truly close because I believe it removes a barrier that many of you have unknowingly placed between yourselves and exactly this kind of answered prayer. Some of you have quietly assumed that genuine breakthrough requires lengthy, eloquent, theologically sophisticated prayer, hours of dedicated intercession before God takes a request seriously. Jabez's entire recorded prayer fits into a single sentence. It required no elaborate preamble, no extended explanation of his circumstances, no carefully constructed theological argument for why he deserved what he was asking for. Father, in the name of Jesus, we ask this morning that everyone connected to this prayer who has felt disqualified from genuine breakthrough because their own prayer life feels too simple, too brief, too unpolished compared to more experienced believers around them would receive genuine freedom from that specific comparison. Matthew chapter 6:7 reminds us not to use vain repetitions as the heathen do, for they think they shall be heard for their much speaking. Length and eloquence were never the actual currency of effective prayer. Genuine direct honesty has always been sufficient. Let the declaration rise now over this final freedom. I declare that my own brief simple prayers carry the same weight Jabez's brief simple prayer carried, regardless of how unpolished or unsophisticated they may feel compared to prayers I have heard from others. I declare that God responds to genuine directness rather than impressive length, and I release myself from any remaining pressure to perform eloquence I do not actually possess in order to be genuinely heard in the name of Jesus. As we arrive now at the genuine conclusion of this ministration, I want to bring us back full circle to exactly where we began. We began this morning with a name given in sorrow, spoken over a child by a mother who could not have known that child would one day surpass every brother who shared his same painful family history. We began with a discovery that a name given in someone else's pain does not carry final authority over what a person is permitted to become. Everything else prayed this morning, the destiny restoration, the family deliverance, the marriage breakthrough, the financial gates, the healing, the covenant breaking, the angelic intervention, the witchcraft destruction, the time and virtue restored, the divine preservation, every specific word of knowledge, all of it flows directly out of that single foundational reality established at the very beginning. A person who genuinely calls the way Jabez called, rather than passively accepting whatever trajectory their name or history seems to prophesy, naturally receives everything subsequently needed. Not because they have manipulated God into compliance through sufficiently intense prayer, but because that posture itself, sustained and genuine, produces the fourfold granting Jabez himself received. I want to ask you directly one final time before we close. Will you actually call the way Jabez called, specifically, boldly, asking for all four things at once rather than settling for whichever single request felt safest to voice? The real test will not be measured by how you feel in this exact moment. It will be measured by whether you actually open your mouth and ask for blessing indeed, enlarge coasts, God's sustained hand, and [clears throat] protection from grief-producing evil, rather than continuing to quietly accept whatever smaller portion your own painful history has trained you to expect instead. Let the final declaration of this entire ministration rise now, complete and sealed. I declare that whatever name has been spoken over me in sorrow does not determine my final destination. I declare that my own cry this morning, however simply expressed, carries the same authority Jabez's brief direct prayer once carried. Go now in the name of Jesus carrying blessing indeed, enlarge coasts, the sustained hand of God, and protection from grief-producing evil into the remainder of this day and every day beyond it. And God granted him that which he requested. Let it be granted to you exactly the same way. Amen.
